mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000K units signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% signals a deep liquidity-driven easing, which boosts risk appetite and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during such PAYEMS accelerations.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a precautionary savings shift, which often precedes a demand slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS quarterly change > 0% AND GDPC1 quarterly change < -1% in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during such INDPRO expansions.
